Each new identity must space its first transactions according to a per-epoch cipher derived from the prior block hash, so agents cannot batch registrations without visible gaps. Traffic that arrives faster than the schedule is queued and its sender flagged, forcing an attacker to stretch each fake identity across real wall-clock time. The onyx ledger records missed slots, and every sybil must pay that delay in parallel workers, multiplying coordination cost by the number of identities sustained.
